changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For teams replacing a homegrown billing system, lead with engineering time recovered instead of revenue growth: 'Stop billing being a tax on the roadmap. Pricing changes that take a quarter today take minutes.' Proof point for the demo: changing a price, trials and proration in a few clicks, which the buyer called 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.'
changes.why: The buyer rejected the revenue framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap') and responded to the demo as roadmap time saved, because every pricing change took them a quarter.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a champion asks for payback, position the independent economic impact study as the starting template for building the customer's own number, not as the proof itself: 'We'll build your payback case with you, from your own costs, so you have a number that's ours to take to finance.' Offer the working session within days of the payback ask.
changes.why: The champion asked 'do you have something that shows payback?' and then said he couldn't get past the CFO 'without a number that's ours'; the session to build that number never happened, and the rep named their own number as the missing proof.

changes.change: Add a CFO-facing cost-of-the-status-quo line for homegrown-billing prospects, delivered to finance before the proposal goes out: put a dollar figure on the tax on the roadmap by adding up engineering quarters spent per pricing change, the risk of a system whose builder has left, and subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it (pair this last item with M10 smart retries). The goal is to make the problem read as 'on fire' rather than 'nice to have'.
changes.why: Finance saw the project as 'nice to have' and, as relayed secondhand through the champion, 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded'. The cost ingredients (quarter-long pricing changes, the builder gone, failed-card lapses) were on the table but were never added up, and the CFO never heard our case directly.

changes.change: Add a migration proof point for billing replacements: a reference customer, where we have one, who moved existing subscriptions without asking their customers for card details again and did it in stages. Offer a conversation with that customer, not only a document.
changes.why: The buyer's migration concern was moving subscriptions without re-collecting card details and doing it in stages; when offered a doc, he 'wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.'
